findings.issue: The table-build timing (SPEC-11/SPEC-12, §9 'Start-up') times a third call to buildEvaluatorTables() after 2M evaluate calls, when the JIT is already warm. The start-up cost the spec cares about is the first, cold build at module load, which is slower.
findings.evidence: Plain Node 22.18.0 in the scratchpad: cold import+build about 41 ms (this includes type stripping), and a second build about 26 ms. The test reports 24.8 ms. The cold build still meets the 50 ms target, so nothing is broken today, but the test would not notice the cold build going past 50 ms while the warm rebuild stays under.
findings.fix: Time the build first in the test, before any evaluate warm-up. Or, better, record performance.now() around the module-level build in a fresh worker/dynamic import (test side only). At minimum, move the buildStart/buildEvaluatorTables() block to the top of the test so it runs before evaluateAll.

findings.issue: The module-level scratch arrays (rankCounts/suitMasks/suitCounts) clash with the literal wording of the §5 invariant 'The module holds no mutable state after load'. However, §5 algorithm step 1 explicitly allows 'module-level scratch typed arrays that are reset on each call'. The arrays are reset at the start of every call, and evaluate is synchronous and never re-enters itself, so no state can be observed across calls and purity holds. The test at hand-evaluator.test.ts:34 checks that a call after a rejected one is still correct. I judge this acceptable.
findings.evidence: spec.md §5 step 1 vs the Invariants bullet; hand-evaluator.ts:163-173.
findings.fix: No code change. Optionally clarify the spec invariant to 'no observable mutable state' when the spec is next edited.

findings.issue: The 'two sets of trips' case repeats acceptance SPEC-04 case (b) almost exactly (the same 7 cards).
findings.evidence: acceptance.test.ts:144 uses 9s 9h | 9d 4c 4s 4h Kc, the same hand.
findings.fix: Drop the duplicate assertion, or replace it with a different hand shape (e.g. trips plus two pairs).

summary: The implementation matches the spec. The evaluator uses a flush table plus a quinary-indexed non-flush table, and dense ranks come from sorting packed scores. The exhaustive 2,598,960-hand test against an independent oracle (classKey is a unique base-5 encoding; the wheel and category order are right) makes the core tests strong: any ranking mutation fails AC#1. Error messages match §5 exactly. I re-ran the SPEC-12 command: 15.9M evals/s, 24.8 ms build, pass. The SPEC-14 grep is clean. The tests/engine suite passes. The scratch arrays are acceptable under §5 step 1. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. One MINOR: the build-time test measures a warm rebuild, not the cold start-up build.
